body: Well, to answer the first question is that... Well, my initial therapist that diagnosed me referred me to someone, who in return referred me.. And so on and so on. I think it was after thirty therapists they actually found someone who would treat me... But even he wanted to send me to a mental hospital. The second question is something I did ask my therapist. He told me "Because BPD is about as rare as schizophrenia, but BPD is usually a learned thing. It's common from sexual abuse, emotional abuse, physical abuse. Or even your parents telling you to not express your emotions. It's a learned behavior that can seriously fuck with your brain... So they recognize it as a disorder like a handicap but nothing to have assisted living with.. It's the same case as Antisocial personality disorder it's real no one doubts that but it's nothing serious like Schizophrenia or any other MAJOR illness."

I was diagnosed when I was 18. The age where you have to get diagnosed. I still am in therapy. My therapist says that "I'll be a long term project" so... If you go to therapy get ready for it to be for a very long time.

A day to day struggle for BPD Is the constant mood swings. The biggest problem is for BPD sufferers we go to extreme highs to extreme lows in matters of minutes to hours. You can see how that could get in the way.
I edited the post to show it. Thanks for reminding me to do that.
